email.body1:
Ben, saw EliseAI close the $250M Series E led by a16z at a $2.2B valuation, with the push deeper into housing and healthcare.

Scaling that fast usually means more enterprise accounts in play than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for EliseAI off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Ben, quick follow-up for EliseAI.

After a raise that size, board expectations on pipeline jump faster than enterprise headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings EliseAI needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Ben, last bit of proof for EliseAI.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how EliseAI's reply rate likely compares to other high-growth AI sellers. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Ben, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise coverage without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The fundraise-to-hiring stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your enterprise motion? I'll tailor it to EliseAI either way.
